source: NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), study search API: https://osdr.nasa.gov/osdr/data/search

findings.finding: Mice that lived on the space station for 33 days lost a lot of muscle and bone.
findings.subjects: Mice on the International Space Station (SpaceX-19 mission, 2019–2020)
findings.note: Astronauts Jessica Meir and Christina Koch, who were on the station at the time, are among the study’s authors.
quotes: Wild type mice lost significant muscle and bone mass during the 33 d spent in microgravity.

citation.studyTitle: Targeting myostatin/activin A protects against skeletal muscle and bone loss during spaceflight [plasma proteomics]
citation.publicationTitle: Targeting myostatin/activin A protects against skeletal muscle and bone loss during spaceflight

findings.finding: Mice in space lost bone, and their blood showed signs that their bones were not being kept in balance. The tiny microbes living in their gut changed too.
findings.subjects: Mice on the International Space Station (Rodent Research 5, SpaceX-11 mission, 2017)
quotes: Along with BMD loss, ELISA analysis reveals increases of osteocalcin and reductions in tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase 5b signifying additional loss of bone homeostasis in flight.

citation.studyTitle: Specific Host Metabolite and Gut Microbiome Alterations Are Associated with Bone-loss During Spaceflight
citation.publicationTitle: Specific host metabolite and gut microbiome alterations are associated with bone loss during spaceflight

findings.finding: Exercising during the 70 days in bed stopped the volunteers losing fitness, muscle, strength and stamina.
findings.subjects: 22 healthy young men in NASA’s 70-day bed-rest study on Earth (lying in bed copies some effects of weightlessness)
quotes: Exercise training during the National Aeronautics and Space Administration 70-d bed rest study effectively counteracted the decline in aerobic capacity, muscle mass, strength, and endurance.

citation.studyTitle: Exercise Training Attenuates the Muscle Mitochondria Genomic Response to Bed Rest (microarray data)
citation.publicationTitle: Exercise Training Attenuates the Muscle Mitochondria Genomic Response to Bed Rest.

findings.finding: Exercise almost cancelled out the changes in how their muscle genes behaved: it cut the number of changed genes by 89% and 96% in the two muscles studied. Extra protein in their food helped much less.
findings.subjects: 24 healthy women in a 60-day bed-rest study on Earth
quotes: Exercise countermeasure demonstrated a drastic compensatory effect, decreasing the number of differentially-expressed genes by 89 and 96% in SOL and VL.

citation.studyTitle: Woman skeletal muscle transcriptome with bed rest and countermeasures.
citation.publicationTitle: Large-scale mRNA analysis of female skeletal muscles during 60 days of bed rest with and without exercise or dietary protein supplementation as countermeasures.

findings.finding: Their thigh muscles got smaller and weaker. Then 21 days of strength exercise brought most of it back.
findings.subjects: 11 healthy young men who kept one leg off the ground for 10 days, on Earth
quotes: QF CSA and MVC decreased with ULLS.
The AR period restored most of these neuromuscular alterations.

citation.studyTitle: Ten-day human unilateral lower limb suspension and active recovery in young healthy men
citation.publicationTitle: Effects of short‐term unloading and active recovery on human motor unit properties, neuromuscular junction transmission and transcriptomic profile

findings.finding: Spaceflight changed the body’s daily clock (the circadian rhythm, which tells us when to feel sleepy) and stressed the tiny power stations inside cells.
findings.subjects: Health data from 59 astronauts, NASA’s Twins Study, and hundreds of samples flown in space
findings.note: This study looked at the body clock, not at sleep itself. Real astronauts plan their sleep carefully because the body clock gets confused in space.
quotes: Additional pathways altered in spaceflight included cell cycle, circadian rhythm, and olfactory activity pathways, all of which are known to have interactions with mitochondrial activity.

citation.studyTitle: Comprehensive multi-omics analysis reveals mitochondrial stress as a central biological hub for spaceflight impact
citation.publicationTitle: Comprehensive Multi-omics Analysis Reveals Mitochondrial Stress as a Central Biological Hub for Spaceflight Impact
citation.authors: Willian A. da Silveira et al.

findings.finding: After the radiation, male mice found it harder to learn their way around a maze. Female mice did not.
findings.subjects: Mice on Earth exposed to particle beams that copy deep-space radiation
quotes: males displayed impaired spatial learning, whereas females did not.

citation.studyTitle: The impact of deep space radiation on cognitive performance: From biological sex to biomarkers to countermeasures (Elevated Plus Maze, Novel Object Recognition, Open Field, Radial Arm Water Maze, and Three Chamber Social Isolation/Interaction)
citation.publicationTitle: The impact of deep space radiation on cognitive performance: From biological sex to biomarkers to countermeasures

findings.finding: Scientists checked the mice’s muscle proteins 9 months after they recovered. The study found a long-term effect on the proteins that help muscles use energy.
findings.subjects: Female mice on Earth: weightlessness copied by lifting their back legs, then a low dose of copied space radiation
quotes: We investigated protein abundance changes 9-months after recovery from combined unloading and radiation exposure.

citation.studyTitle: Low-dose Simulated Galactic Cosmic Radiation Exposure After Hindlimb Unloading Has Long-term Impact on Skeletal Muscle Metabolic Proteins
citation.publicationTitle: Low-dose simulated galactic cosmic radiation exposure after hindlimb unloading has long-term impact on skeletal muscle metabolic proteins in female mice
